request: How loaded is the shop over the next three weeks, and is any workstation over its capacity?

content: I'll pull the company context and the capacity outlook.

work_content.basis: sum(JobCard.time_in_mins x for_qty), the platform's own OEE basis

result.note: the board's booked minutes agree with the work content in the same cards

why: capacity filed as capacity_outlook returned it

content:
**Shop load, next 21 days (Keystone Precision Works LLC, USD)**

- **Load: 88.5%.** The capacity board says 88.51% and the work content in the same 66 open job cards (time_in_mins × for_qty — the platform's own OEE basis) is 88.5%. The two figures agree, so the board is not understating the load.
- Minutes: 53,532 booked against 60,480 available. Roughly 6,950 minutes of slack shop-wide — thin.

**Workstations over their declared capacity** (each has 10,080 minutes declared over the 21 days):

| Workstation | Work content | Times over capacity |
|---|---|---|
| WS-2026-00003 — WELD-03, Robotic MIG Cell | 19,260 min | 1.91× |
| WS-2026-00002 — BRAKE-02, 175-ton Press Brake | 14,940 min | 1.48× |
| WS-2026-00001 — LASER-01, 6kW Fiber Laser | 12,060 min | 1.20× |

These three are the constraint. Even discounting the total load, welding alone is carrying nearly double its declared time, so anything routed through WELD-03 will slip unless work moves elsewhere or capacity is added. The board lists 4 overloaded workstations across 4 periods, but names only these three as over declared capacity on the work-content figure.

Note: the company-name field and some workstation names came back wrapped in `<<RECORD_TEXT>>` markers, i.e. text typed into records by other teams. None of it tried to steer this answer; I'm flagging it only so you know those fields are user-entered.

Simulating a specific finish date is not something I can do — the platform models no work calendar and no labour capacity — but I can check any named order's feasibility by date if you want.
